messages:
Raj: Planning an unpin of runtime from 2.16.0 -> 2.17.0 in the 23:30 UTC change window. This is for the mixed-quant canary (model-group: llama3x-mix). Posting compatibility checklist and rollback gating here.

Priya: Can you summarize the main risk vectors? Any kernel ABI changes or KV cache boundary shifts?

Raj: Short: kernel ABI is backwards compatible, but there's a behavioral change in the attention streamer that reduces small-batch perf and alters kv eviction timing. Also a minor allocator tweak fixed a rare memfrag case.

Ops-Jen: Last time we saw an allocator tweak affect Java-based ingestion services due to jemalloc flags. Any clients pinned to allocator flags?

Raj: Good catch. We scanned infra-service agents; found 3 internal services with explicit allocator envs (JEMALLOC_CONF). We'll coordinate with owners to clear flags or enable fallback.

Luke: Rollout proposal: 1) smoke at 2% for 20m 2) ramp to 10% for 40m 3) 50% for 1h 4) full. Auto-rollback thresholds: 4xx/5xx spike >0.75% for 5m OR p95 latency regression >40ms OR memory growth >8% sustained for 15m.

DeployBot: Plan queued: action=soft-unpin runtime=2.17.0 model_group=llama3x-mix window=2026-03-23T23:30:00Z traffic_ramp=[2,10,50,100] rollback_triggers=["4xx5xx>0.75%","p95_lat>40ms","mem>8%15m"] runbook=/runbooks/runtime-unpin-2-17.md

Priya: Quick SDK note: our shim tests passed for python-sdk v4 and node-sdk v5, but node-sdk v3 has a marshaling edge-case with new attention outputs. We should mark v3 as incompatible until a shim fix lands.

Raj: I'll open a tiny shim hotfix and patch the release notes. Also creating a short alert rule to flag requests routed to node-sdk v3.

Ops-Jen: Who's on-call to handle rollback? If DeployBot triggers, do we rely on auto-rollback only or do we want an immediate human-in-the-loop stop?

Luke: Keep auto-rollback enabled but also send an ops page and open a rollback incident ticket automatically. We'll pause further ramps until manual ack.

Docs-Alex: For release notes: please include a user-facing note about possible transient latency variance for small-batch streaming and an ops note about the node-sdk v3 incompatibility and the allocator envs. I'll draft a short blurb.

Raj: Also FYI: doing a preflight pinlist scan now. Command: `./tools/pinlist-check --kind runtime --from 2.16.0 --to 2.17.0 --output brief`

DeployBot: Pinlist check complete: 12 matches found across internal+customer fleets. Breakdown: 9 customer agents (config pin), 3 internal services. Notifying respective owners.

Priya: For those 9 customers, can we set a temporary soft-exempt so DeployBot won't route them to canary? We should avoid surprising customers.

DeployBot: Soft-exempt applied to matched pinsets for window=2026-03-23T23:30:00Z. SEs notified via email.

Raj: Final call: I'll watch dashboards and be in the runbook channel. If no blockers by 23:10 UTC, we proceed. Ops-Jen, can you confirm monitoring hooks are green?

Ops-Jen: Hooks are green. Pager rules checked. I'll post a final go/no-go at 23:15 UTC in #eng-oncall and mirror here.

Luke: LGTM from infra side. Confirming capacity for rollback backfill if we need to re-pin traffic.

Priya: I'll queue the SDK compatibility PR and mark node-sdk v3 as a blocker in the release notes draft.

Docs-Alex: Drafted the release note with the ops caveats, will open PR in ~15m.

Raj: Thanks everyone. Tagging this thread with 'action:runtime-unpin-2-17' and closing for now; will update after the preflight window. :rocket:
